result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.attracting_components()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Find the attracting components of a directed graph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L56891-L56947){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.attracting_components() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Attracting components](/assets/graphs/attracting-components.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="A directed graph: A points to B and to D, and B and C point to each other. A random walk that leaves A never comes back: it ends up circling B and C or stuck at D. Those are the attracting components, D in the accent color and B, C in teal, listed on the card as {D} and {B, C}; A, in neither, is faded." width="100%"} An attracting component is a strongly connected component with no edges leaving it: once a walk enters, it can never leave. They are the "sinks" of the condensation. In a Markov chain they are the closed communicating classes, which hold all of the long-run probability; in a web or citation graph they are traps for random surfers; in a state machine they are terminal behaviors. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[set[int]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The attracting components as sets of node IDs. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is undirected. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Strongly connected components are found first; a component is attracting when no edge goes from it to another component, $O(V + E)$ in total. Matches NetworkX's `attracting_components`. ## Examples {.doc-examples} A random walk on this graph ends up circling B-C or stuck at D: ::: {#9c5dbe54 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g = ec.Graph(directed=True).add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D"]) g.add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "B"), ("A", "D")]) [sorted(g.get_label_from_id(n) for n in c) for c in g.attracting_components()] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` [['D'], ['B', 'C']] ``` ::: :::
